Identify periods in a. performed music b. notated music

Musical phrases within a passage may sound similar to one another to promote comprehensibility, memorability, and unity, or they may sound dissimilar to one another to create variety, interest, and contrast. Melodic relationships that result may be represented by lowercase letters. The most common are Bullet a a – denotes a phrase and its literal repetition Bulleta a’ – denotes a phrase and a varied repetition Bullet a b – denotes two phrases that are melodically contrasting

Two phrases may combine into a period, in which the first phrase, called the antecedent, ends with an inconclusive cadence and the second phrase, called the consequent, provides stronger harmonic repose with a conclusive cadence. A parallel period consists of two phrases that are melodically similar; a contrasting period consists of two phrases that are melodically contrasting.

learning_objectives.statement: Identify common sections in a. performed music b. notated music

Common sections within a piece of music include the introduction, interlude, bridge, verse, refrain, chorus, coda, and codetta.

include: Interpret the rate of change at an instant in terms of average rates of change over intervals containing that instant.
Calculus uses limits to understand and model dynamic change.

Because an average rate of change divides the change in one variable by the change in another, the average rate of change is undefined at a point where the change in the independent variable would be zero.
The limit concept allows us to define instantaneous rate of change in terms of average rates of change.

learning_objectives.title: Defining Limits and Using Limit Notation
learning_objectives.statement: Represent limits analytically using correct notation. Interpret limits expressed in analytic notation.
include: Represent limits analytically using correct notation.
Interpret limits expressed in analytic notation.

Given a function f, the limit of f (x) as x approaches c is a real number R if f (x) can be made arbitrarily close to R by taking x sufficiently close to c (but not equal to c). If the limit exists and is a real number, then the common notation is lim f x( ) = R.
A limit can be expressed in multiple ways, including graphically, numerically, and analytically.
exclude: The epsilon-delta definition of a limit is not assessed on the AP Calculus AB or BC Exam. However, teachers may include this topic in the course if time permits.

learning_objectives.title: Estimating Limit Values from Graphs
learning_objectives.statement: Estimate limits of functions.
include: Estimate limits of functions.
The concept of a limit includes one sided limits.
Graphical information about a function can be used to estimate limits.
Because of issues of scale, graphical representations of functions may miss important function behavior.

A limit might not exist for some functions at particular values of x. Some ways that the limit might not exist are if the function is unbounded, if the function is oscillating near this value, or if the limit from the left does not equal the limit from the right.

learning_objectives.title: Estimating Limit Values from Tables
learning_objectives.statement: Estimate limits of functions.
include: Estimate limits of functions.
Numerical information can be used to estimate limits.

learning_objectives.title: Determining Limits Using Algebraic Properties of Limits
learning_objectives.statement: Determine the limits of functions using limit theorems.
include: Determine the limits of functions using limit theorems.
One-sided limits can be determined analytically or graphically.
Limits of sums, differences, products, quotients, and composite functions can be found using limit theorems.

learning_objectives.title: Determining Limits Using Algebraic Manipulation
learning_objectives.statement: Determine the limits of functions using equivalent expressions for the function or the squeeze theorem.
include: Determine the limits of functions using equivalent expressions for the function or the squeeze theorem.
necessary or helpful to rearrange expressions into equivalent forms before evaluating limits.

learning_objectives.title: Selecting Procedures for Determining Limits
learning_objectives.statement: This topic is intended to focus on the skill of selecting an appropriate procedure for determining limits. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to determining limits.
include: This topic is intended to focus on the skill of selecting an appropriate procedure for determining limits. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to determining limits.

learning_objectives.title: Determining Limits Using the Squeeze Theorem
learning_objectives.statement: Determine the limits of functions using equivalent expressions for the function or the squeeze theorem.
include: Determine the limits of functions using equivalent expressions for the function or the squeeze theorem.
The limit of a function may be found by using the squeeze theorem.

learning_objectives.title: Connecting Multiple Representations of Limits
learning_objectives.statement: This topic is intended to focus on connecting representations. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to limits and translating mathematical information from a single representation or across multiple representations.
include: This topic is intended to focus on connecting representations. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to limits and translating mathematical information from a single representation or across multiple representations.

learning_objectives.title: Exploring Types of Discontinuities
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about continuity at a point using the definition.
include: Justify conclusions about continuity at a point using the definition.
Types of discontinuities include removable discontinuities, jump discontinuities, and discontinuities due to vertical asymptotes.

learning_objectives.title: Defining Continuity at a Point
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about continuity at a point using the definition.
include: Justify conclusions about continuity at a point using the definition.
A function f is continuous at x equals c provided that f of c exists,lim right arrow c of f of x exists, andlim over x right arrow c of f of x equals f of c

learning_objectives.title: Confirming Continuity over an Interval
learning_objectives.statement: Determine intervals over which a function is continuous.
include: Determine intervals over which a function is continuous.
A function is continuous on an interval if the function is continuous at each point in the interval.
Polynomial, rational, power, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions are continuous on all points in their domains.

learning_objectives.title: Removing Discontinuities
learning_objectives.statement: Determine values of x or solve for parameters that make discontinuous functions continuous, if possible.
include: Determine values of x or solve for parameters that make discontinuous functions continuous, if possible.

If the limit of a function exists at a discontinuity in its graph, then it is possible to remove the discontinuity by defining or redefining the value of the function at that point, so it equals the value of the limit of the function as x approaches that point.

In order for a piecewise-defined function to be continuous at a boundary to the partition of its domain, the value of the expression defining the function on one side of the boundary must equal the value of the expression defining the other side of the boundary, as well as the value of the function at the boundary.

learning_objectives.title: Connecting Infinite Limits and Vertical Asymptotes
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret the behavior of functions using limits involving infinity.
include: Interpret the behavior of functions using limits involving infinity.
The concept of a limit can be extended to include infinite limits.
Asymptotic and unbounded behavior of functions can be described and explained using limits.

learning_objectives.title: Connecting Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret the behavior of functions using limits involving infinity.
include: Interpret the behavior of functions using limits involving infinity.
The concept of a limit can be extended to include limits at infinity.
Limits at infinity describe end behavior.
Relative magnitudes of functions and their rates of change can be compared using limits.

learning_objectives.statement: Represent the derivative of a function as the limit of a difference quotient. Determine the equation of a line tangent to a curve at a given point.
include: Represent the derivative of a function as the limit of a difference quotient.
Determine the equation of a line tangent to a curve at a given point.

learning_objectives.title: Estimating Derivatives of a Function at a Point
learning_objectives.statement: Estimate derivatives.
include: Estimate derivatives.
The derivative at a point can be estimated from information given in tables or graphs.
Technology can be used to calculate or estimate the value of a derivative of a function at a point.

learning_objectives.title: Connecting Differentiability and Continuity: Determining When Derivatives Do and Do Not Exist
learning_objectives.statement: Explain the relationship between differentiability and continuity.
include: Explain the relationship between differentiability and continuity.
If a function is differentiable at a point, then it is continuous at that point. In particular, if a point is not in the domain of f, then it is not in the domain of f '.
A continuous function may fail to be differentiable at a point in its domain.

learning_objectives.title: Applying the Power Rule
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions.
Direct application of the definition of the derivative and specific rules can be used to calculate the derivative for functions of the form equals x to the r-th power r.

learning_objectives.title: Derivative Rules: Constant, Sum, Difference, and Constant Multiple
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions.
Sums, differences, and constant multiples of functions can be differentiated using derivative rules.
The power rule combined with sum, difference, and constant multiple properties can be used to find the derivatives for polynomial functions.

learning_objectives.title: Derivatives of cos x, sin x, ex, and ln x
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions. Interpret a limit as a definition of a derivative.
include: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions.
Interpret a limit as a definition of a derivative.
Specific rules can be used to find the derivatives for sine, cosine, exponential, and logarithmic functions.
In some cases, recognizing an expression for the definition of the derivative of a function whose derivative is known offers a strategy for determining a limit.

learning_objectives.title: The Product Rule
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
Derivatives of products of differentiable functions can be found using the product rule.

learning_objectives.title: The Quotient Rule
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
Derivatives of quotients of differentiable functions can be found using the quotient rule.

learning_objectives.title: Finding the Derivatives of Tangent, Cotangent, Secant, and/or Cosecant Functions
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
Rearranging tangent, cotangent, secant, and cosecant functions using identities allows differentiation using derivative rules.

topics.name: Differentiation: Composite, Implicit, and Inverse Functions

learning_objectives.title: The Chain Rule
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of compositions of differentiable functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of compositions of differentiable functions.
The chain rule provides a way to differentiate composite functions.

learning_objectives.title: Implicit Differentiation
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of implicitly defined functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of implicitly defined functions.
The chain rule is the basis for implicit differentiation.

learning_objectives.title: Differentiating Inverse Functions
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of inverse and inverse trigonometric functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of inverse and inverse trigonometric functions.
The chain rule and definition of an inverse function can be used to find the derivative of an inverse function, provided the derivative exists.

learning_objectives.title: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of inverse and inverse trigonometric functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of inverse and inverse trigonometric functions.
The chain rule applied with the definition of an inverse function, or the formula for the derivative of an inverse function, can be used to find the derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions.

learning_objectives.title: Selecting Procedures for Calculating Derivatives
learning_objectives.statement: This topic is intended to focus on the skill of selecting an appropriate procedure for calculating derivatives. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to calculating derivatives.
include: This topic is intended to focus on the skill of selecting an appropriate procedure for calculating derivatives. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to calculating derivatives.

learning_objectives.title: Calculating Higher - Order Derivatives
learning_objectives.statement: Determine higher order derivatives of a function.
include: Determine higher order derivatives of a function.
Differentiating f ′ produces the second derivative f ″, provided the derivative of f ′ exists; repeating this process produces higherorder derivatives of f .

Higher-order derivatives are represented with a variety of notations. For y equals f of x), notations for the second derivative include d s quared y over d x squared comma f prime prime of x and y ″. Higher-order derivatives can be denoted n-th power y over d x to the n-th power.

learning_objectives.title: Interpreting the Meaning of the Derivative in Context
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret the meaning of a derivative in context.
include: Interpret the meaning of a derivative in context.
The derivative of a function can be interpreted as the instantaneous rate of change with respect to its independent variable.
The derivative can be used to express information about rates of change in applied contexts.
The unit for f'(x) is the unit for f divided by the unit for x.

learning_objectives.title: Straight-Line Motion: Connecting Position, Velocity, and Acceleration
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate rates of change in applied contexts.
include: Calculate rates of change in applied contexts.
The derivative can be used to solve rectilinear motion problems involving position, speed, velocity, and acceleration.

learning_objectives.title: Rates of Change in Applied Contexts Other Than Motion
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret rates of change in applied contexts.
include: Interpret rates of change in applied contexts.
The derivative can be used to solve problems involving rates of change in applied contexts.

learning_objectives.title: Introduction to Related Rates
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate related rates in applied contexts.
include: Calculate related rates in applied contexts.
The chain rule is the basis for differentiating variables in a related rates problem with respect to the same independent variable.
Other differentiation rules, such as the product rule and the quotient rule, may also be necessary to differentiate all variables with respect to the same independent variable.

learning_objectives.title: Solving Related Rates Problems
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret related rates in applied contexts.
include: Interpret related rates in applied contexts.
The derivative can be used to solve related rates problems; that is, finding a rate at which one quantity is changing by relating it to other quantities whose rates of change are known.

learning_objectives.title: Approximating Values of a Function Using Local Linearity and Linearization
learning_objectives.statement: Approximate a value on a curve using the equation of a tangent line. Determine limits of functions that result in indeterminate forms.
include: Approximate a value on a curve using the equation of a tangent line.
Determine limits of functions that result in indeterminate forms.
The tangent line is the graph of a locally linear approximation of the function near the point of tangency.

For a tangent line approximation, the function’s behavior near the point of tangency may determine whether a tangent line value is an underestimate or an overestimate of the corresponding function value.
When the ratio of two functions tends to 0 over fraction with numerator normal infinity and denominator normal infinityin the limit, such forms are said to be indeterminate.
Limits of the indeterminate forms 0 over e fraction with numerator normal infinity and denominator normal infinitymay be evaluated using L’Hospital’s Rule.

learning_objectives.title: Using the Mean Value Theorem
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about functions by applying the Mean Value Theorem over an interval.
include: Justify conclusions about functions by applying the Mean Value Theorem over an interval.

If a function f is continuous over the interval [a, b] and differentiable over the interval (a, b), then the Mean Value Theorem guarantees a point within that open interval where the instantaneous rate of change equals the average rate of change over the interval.

learning_objectives.title: Extreme Value Theorem, Global Versus Local Extrema, and Critical Points
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about functions by applying the Extreme Value Theorem.
include: Justify conclusions about functions by applying the Extreme Value Theorem.
If a function f is continuous over the interval [a, b], then the Extreme Value Theorem guarantees that f has at least one minimum value and at least one maximum value on [a, b].
A point on a function where the first derivative equals zero or fails to exist is a critical point of the function.
All local (relative) extrema occur at critical points of a function, though not all critical points are local extrema.

learning_objectives.title: Determining Intervals on Which a Function Is Increasing or Decreasing
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
The first derivative of a function can provide information about the function and its graph, including intervals where the function is increasing or decreasing.

learning_objectives.title: Using the First Derivative Test to Determine Relative (Local) Extrema
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
The first derivative of a function can determine the location of relative (local) extrema of the function.

learning_objectives.title: Using the Candidates Test to Determine Absolute (Global) Extrema
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
Absolute (global) extrema of a function on a closed interval can only occur at critical points or at endpoints.

learning_objectives.title: Determining Concavity of Functions over Their Domains
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
The graph of a function is concave up (down) on an open interval if the function’s derivative is increasing (decreasing) on that interval.
The second derivative of a function provides information about the function and its graph, including intervals of upward or downward concavity.
The second derivative of a function may be used to locate points of inflection for the graph of the original function.

learning_objectives.title: Using the Second Derivative Test to Determine Extrema
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
The second derivative of a function may determine whether a critical point is the location of a relative (local) maximum or minimum.

When a continuous function has only one critical point on an interval on its domain and the critical point corresponds to a relative (local) extremum of the function on the interval, then that critical point also corresponds to the absolute (global) extremum of the function on the interval.

learning_objectives.title: Sketching Graphs of Functions and Their Derivatives
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
Key features of functions and their derivatives can be identified and related to their graphical, numerical, and analytical representations.
Graphical, numerical, and analytical information from f' and f" can be used to predict and explain the behavior of f.

learning_objectives.title: Connecting a Function, Its First Derivative, and Its Second Derivative
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
Key features of the graphs of f, f', and f" are related to one another.

learning_objectives.title: Introduction to Optimization Problems
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate minimum and maximum values in applied contexts or analysis of functions.
include: Calculate minimum and maximum values in applied contexts or analysis of functions.
The derivative can be used to solve optimization problems; that is, finding a minimum or maximum value of a function on a given interval.

learning_objectives.title: Solving Optimization Problems
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret minimum and maximum values calculated in applied contexts.
include: Interpret minimum and maximum values calculated in applied contexts.
Minimum and maximum values of a function take on specific meanings in applied contexts.

learning_objectives.title: Exploring Behaviors of Implicit Relations
learning_objectives.statement: Determine critical points of implicit relations. Justify conclusions about the behavior of an implicitly defined function based on evidence from its derivatives.
include: Determine critical points of implicit relations.
Justify conclusions about the behavior of an implicitly defined function based on evidence from its derivatives.
A point on an implicit relation where the first derivative equals zero or does not exist is a critical point of the function.
Applications of derivatives can be extended to implicitly defined functions.
Second derivatives involving implicit differentiation may be relations of x, y, and d

learning_objectives.title: Exploring Accumulations of Change
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret the meaning of areas associated with the graph of a rate of change in context.
include: Interpret the meaning of areas associated with the graph of a rate of change in context.
The area of the region between the graph of a rate of change function and the x axis gives the accumulation of change.
In some cases, accumulation of change can be evaluated by using geometry.
If a rate of change is positive (negative) over an interval, then the accumulated change is positive (negative).
The unit for the area of a region defined by rate of change is the unit for the rate of change multiplied by the unit for the independent variable.

learning_objectives.title: Approximating Areas with Riemann Sums
learning_objectives.statement: Approximate a definite integral using geometric and numerical methods.
include: Approximate a definite integral using geometric and numerical methods.
Definite integrals can be approximated for functions that are represented graphically, numerically, analytically, and verbally.

Definite integrals can be approximated using a left Riemann sum, a right Riemann sum, a midpoint Riemann sum, or a trapezoidal sum; approximations can be computed using either uniform or nonuniform partitions.
Definite integrals can be approximated using numerical methods, with or without technology.

In some cases, a definite integral can be evaluated by using geometry and the connection between the definite integral and area.

Properties of definite integrals include the integral of a constant times a function, the integral of the sum of two functions, reversal of limits of integration, and the integral of a function over adjacent intervals.

Some differential equations can be solved by separation of variables.
Antidifferentiation can be used to find general solutions to differential equations.

learning_objectives.statement: Determine values for positions and rates of change using definite integrals in problems involving rectilinear motion.
include: Determine values for positions and rates of change using definite integrals in problems involving rectilinear motion.

For a particle in rectilinear motion over an interval of time, the definite integral of velocity represents the particle’s displacement over the interval of time, and the definite integral of speed represents the particle’s total distance traveled over the interval of time.

learning_objectives.title: Using Accumulation Functions and Definite Integrals in Applied Contexts
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret the meaning of a definite integral in accumulation problems. Determine net change using definite integrals in applied contexts.
include: Interpret the meaning of a definite integral in accumulation problems.
Determine net change using definite integrals in applied contexts.
A function defined as an integral represents an accumulation of a rate of change.
The definite integral of the rate of change of a quantity over an interval gives the net change of that quantity over that interval.
The definite integral can be used to express information about accumulation and net change in many applied contexts.

learning_objectives.title: Finding the Area Between Curves Expressed as Functions of x
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate areas in the plane using the definite integral.
include: Calculate areas in the plane using the definite integral.
Areas of regions in the plane can be calculated with definite integrals.

learning_objectives.title: Finding the Area Between Curves Expressed as Functions of y
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate areas in the plane using the definite integral.
include: Calculate areas in the plane using the definite integral.
Areas of regions in the plane can be calculated using functions of either x or y.

learning_objectives.title: Finding the Area Between Curves That Intersect at More Than Two Points
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate areas in the plane using the definite integral.
include: Calculate areas in the plane using the definite integral.
Areas of certain regions in the plane may be calculated using a sum of two or more definite integrals or by evaluating a definite integral of the absolute value of the difference of two functions.

learning_objectives.title: Volumes with Cross Sections: Squares and Rectangles
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate volumes of solids with known cross sections using definite integrals.
include: Calculate volumes of solids with known cross sections using definite integrals.
Volumes of solids with square and rectangular cross sections can be found using definite integrals and the area formulas for these shapes.

learning_objectives.title: Volumes with Cross Sections: Triangles and Semicircles
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate volumes of solids with known cross sections using definite integrals.
include: Calculate volumes of solids with known cross sections using definite integrals.
Volumes of solids with triangular cross sections can be found using definite integrals and the area formulas for these shapes.
Volumes of solids with semicircular and other geometrically defined cross sections can be found using definite integrals and the area formulas for these shapes.

learning_objectives.title: Volume with Disc Method: Revolving Around the x- or y-Axis
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate volumes of solids of revolution using definite integrals.
include: Calculate volumes of solids of revolution using definite integrals.
Volumes of solids of revolution around the x- or y-axis may be found by using definite integrals with the disc method.

learning_objectives.title: Volume with Disc Method: Revolving Around Other Axes
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate volumes of solids of revolution using definite integrals.
include: Calculate volumes of solids of revolution using definite integrals.
Volumes of solids of revolution around any horizontal or vertical line in the plane may be found by using definite integrals with the disc method.

learning_objectives.title: Volume with Washer Method: Revolving Around the x- or y-Axis
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate volumes of solids of revolution using definite integrals.
include: Calculate volumes of solids of revolution using definite integrals.
Volumes of solids of revolution around the x- or y-axis whose cross sections are ring shaped may be found using definite integrals with the washer method.

learning_objectives.title: Volume with Washer Method: Revolving Around Other Axes
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate volumes of solids of revolution using definite integrals.
include: Calculate volumes of solids of revolution using definite integrals.
Volumes of solids of revolution around any horizontal or vertical line whose cross sections are ring shaped may be found using definite integrals with the washer method.

learning_objectives.title: Introducing Calculus: Can Change Occur at an Instant?
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret the rate of change at an instant in terms of average rates of change over intervals containing that instant.
include: Interpret the rate of change at an instant in terms of average rates of change over intervals containing that instant.
Calculus uses limits to understand and model dynamic change.

Because an average rate of change divides the change in one variable by the change in another, the average rate of change is undefined at a point where the change in the independent variable would be zero.
The limit concept allows us to define instantaneous rate of change in terms of average rates of change.

learning_objectives.title: Defining Limits and Using Limit Notation
learning_objectives.statement: Represent limits analytically using correct notation. Interpret limits expressed in analytic notation.
include: Represent limits analytically using correct notation.
Interpret limits expressed in analytic notation.

Given a function f, the limit of f (x) as x approaches c is a real number R if f (x) can be made arbitrarily close to R by taking x sufficiently close to c (but not equal to c). If the limit exists and is a real number, then the common notation is lim f x( ) = R.
A limit can be expressed in multiple ways, including graphically, numerically, and analytically.
exclude: The epsilon-delta definition of a limit is not assessed on the AP Calculus AB or BC Exam. However, teachers may include this topic in the course if time permits.

learning_objectives.title: Estimating Limit Values from Graphs
learning_objectives.statement: Estimate limits of functions.
include: Estimate limits of functions.
The concept of a limit includes one sided limits.
Graphical information about a function can be used to estimate limits.
Because of issues of scale, graphical representations of functions may miss important function behavior.

A limit might not exist for some functions at particular values of x. Some ways that the limit might not exist are if the function is unbounded, if the function is oscillating near this value, or if the limit from the left does not equal the limit from the right.

learning_objectives.title: Estimating Limit Values from Tables
learning_objectives.statement: Estimate limits of functions.
include: Estimate limits of functions.
Numerical information can be used to estimate limits.

learning_objectives.title: Determining Limits Using Algebraic Properties of Limits
learning_objectives.statement: Determine the limits of functions using limit theorems.
include: Determine the limits of functions using limit theorems.
One-sided limits can be determined analytically or graphically.
Limits of sums, differences, products, quotients, and composite functions can be found using limit theorems.

learning_objectives.title: Determining Limits Using Algebraic Manipulation
learning_objectives.statement: Determine the limits of functions using equivalent expressions for the function or the squeeze theorem.
include: Determine the limits of functions using equivalent expressions for the function or the squeeze theorem.
necessary or helpful to rearrange expressions into equivalent forms before evaluating limits.

learning_objectives.title: Selecting Procedures for Determining Limits
learning_objectives.statement: This topic is intended to focus on the skill of selecting an appropriate procedure for determining limits. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to determining limits.
include: This topic is intended to focus on the skill of selecting an appropriate procedure for determining limits. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to determining limits.

learning_objectives.title: Determining Limits Using the Squeeze Theorem
learning_objectives.statement: Determine the limits of functions using equivalent expressions for the function or the squeeze theorem.
include: Determine the limits of functions using equivalent expressions for the function or the squeeze theorem.
The limit of a function may be found by using the squeeze theorem.

learning_objectives.title: Connecting Multiple Representations of Limits
learning_objectives.statement: This topic is intended to focus on connecting representations. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to limits and translating mathematical information from a single representation or across multiple representations.
include: This topic is intended to focus on connecting representations. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to limits and translating mathematical information from a single representation or across multiple representations.

learning_objectives.title: Exploring Types of Discontinuities
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about continuity at a point using the definition.
include: Justify conclusions about continuity at a point using the definition.
Types of discontinuities include removable discontinuities, jump discontinuities, and discontinuities due to vertical asymptotes.

learning_objectives.title: Defining Continuity at a Point
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about continuity at a point using the definition.
include: Justify conclusions about continuity at a point using the definition.
A function f is continuous at x equals c provided that f of c exists,lim right arrow c of f of x exists, andlim over x right arrow c of f of x equals f of c

learning_objectives.title: Confirming Continuity over an Interval
learning_objectives.statement: Determine intervals over which a function is continuous.
include: Determine intervals over which a function is continuous.
A function is continuous on an interval if the function is continuous at each point in the interval.
Polynomial, rational, power, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions are continuous on all points in their domains.

learning_objectives.title: Removing Discontinuities
learning_objectives.statement: Determine values of x or solve for parameters that make discontinuous functions continuous, if possible.
include: Determine values of x or solve for parameters that make discontinuous functions continuous, if possible.

If the limit of a function exists at a discontinuity in its graph, then it is possible to remove the discontinuity by defining or redefining the value of the function at that point, so it equals the value of the limit of the function as x approaches that point.

In order for a piecewise-defined function to be continuous at a boundary to the partition of its domain, the value of the expression defining the function on one side of the boundary must equal the value of the expression defining the other side of the boundary, as well as the value of the function at the boundary.

learning_objectives.title: Connecting Infinite Limits and Vertical Asymptotes
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret the behavior of functions using limits involving infinity.
include: Interpret the behavior of functions using limits involving infinity.
The concept of a limit can be extended to include infinite limits.
Asymptotic and unbounded behavior of functions can be described and explained using limits.

learning_objectives.title: Connecting Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret the behavior of functions using limits involving infinity.
include: Interpret the behavior of functions using limits involving infinity.
The concept of a limit can be extended to include limits at infinity.
Limits at infinity describe end behavior.
Relative magnitudes of functions and their rates of change can be compared using limits.

learning_objectives.title: Working with the Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT)
learning_objectives.statement: Explain the behavior of a function on an interval using the Intermediate Value Theorem. .1 If f is a continuous function on the closed interval [a, b] and d is a number between f (a) and f (b), then the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees that there is at least one number c between a and b, such thatf of c equals d.
include: Explain the behavior of a function on an interval using the Intermediate Value Theorem. .1 If f is a continuous function on the closed interval [a, b] and d is a number between f (a) and f (b), then the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees that there is at least one number c between a and b, such thatf of c equals d.

learning_objectives.title: Defining Average and Instantaneous Rates of Change at a Point
learning_objectives.statement: Determine average rates of change using difference quotients. Represent the derivative of a function as the limit of a difference quotient.
include: Determine average rates of change using difference quotients.
Represent the derivative of a function as the limit of a difference quotient.

The difference quotients t h e fraction with numerator f of open paren a plus h close paren minus f of a and denominator t h e fraction with numerator f of x minus f of a and denominator x minus a express the average rate of change of a function over an interval.

The instantaneous rate of change of a function at x a = can be expressed arrow 0 of the fraction with numerator f of open paren a plus h close paren minus f of a and denominator period orl im over x right arrow a of the fraction with numerator f of x minus f of a and denominator x minus a provided the limit exists. These are equivalent forms of the definition of the derivative and are denoted f '( ) a .

learning_objectives.title: Defining the Derivative of a Function and Using Derivative Notation
learning_objectives.statement: Represent the derivative of a function as the limit of a difference quotient. Determine the equation of a line tangent to a curve at a given point.
include: Represent the derivative of a function as the limit of a difference quotient.
Determine the equation of a line tangent to a curve at a given point.
The derivative of f is the function whose value at x islim over h right arrow 0 of the fraction with numerator f of open paren x plus h close paren minus f of x and denominator , provided this limit

The derivative can be represented graphically, numerically, analytically, and verbally.
The derivative of a function at a point is the slope of the line tangent to a graph of the function at that point.

learning_objectives.title: Estimating Derivatives of a Function at a Point
learning_objectives.statement: Estimate derivatives.
include: Estimate derivatives.
The derivative at a point can be estimated from information given in tables or graphs.
Technology can be used to calculate or estimate the value of a derivative of a function at a point.

learning_objectives.title: Connecting Differentiability and Continuity: Determining When Derivatives Do and Do Not Exist
learning_objectives.statement: Explain the relationship between differentiability and continuity.
include: Explain the relationship between differentiability and continuity.
If a function is differentiable at a point, then it is continuous at that point. In particular, if a point is not in the domain of f, then it is not in the domain of f '.
A continuous function may fail to be differentiable at a point in its domain.

learning_objectives.title: Applying the Power Rule
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions.
Direct application of the definition of the derivative and specific rules can be used to calculate the derivative for functions of the form equals x to the r-th power r.

learning_objectives.title: Derivative Rules: Constant, Sum, Difference, and Constant Multiple
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions.
Sums, differences, and constant multiples of functions can be differentiated using derivative rules.
The power rule combined with sum, difference, and constant multiple properties can be used to find the derivatives for polynomial functions.

learning_objectives.title: Derivatives of cos x, sin x, ex, and ln x
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions. Interpret a limit as a definition of a derivative.
include: Calculate derivatives of familiar functions.
Interpret a limit as a definition of a derivative.
Specific rules can be used to find the derivatives for sine, cosine, exponential, and logarithmic functions.
In some cases, recognizing an expression for the definition of the derivative of a function whose derivative is known offers a strategy for determining a limit.

learning_objectives.title: The Product Rule
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
Derivatives of products of differentiable functions can be found using the product rule.

learning_objectives.title: The Quotient Rule
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
Derivatives of quotients of differentiable functions can be found using the quotient rule.

learning_objectives.title: Finding the Derivatives of Tangent, Cotangent, Secant, and/or Cosecant Functions
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of products and quotients of differentiable functions.
Rearranging tangent, cotangent, secant, and cosecant functions using identities allows differentiation using derivative rules.

topics.name: Differentiation: Composite, Implicit, and Inverse Functions

learning_objectives.title: The Chain Rule
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of compositions of differentiable functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of compositions of differentiable functions.
The chain rule provides a way to differentiate composite functions.

learning_objectives.title: Implicit Differentiation
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of implicitly defined functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of implicitly defined functions.
The chain rule is the basis for implicit differentiation.

learning_objectives.title: Differentiating Inverse Functions
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of inverse and inverse trigonometric functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of inverse and inverse trigonometric functions.
The chain rule and definition of an inverse function can be used to find the derivative of an inverse function, provided the derivative exists.

learning_objectives.title: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate derivatives of inverse and inverse trigonometric functions.
include: Calculate derivatives of inverse and inverse trigonometric functions.
The chain rule applied with the definition of an inverse function, or the formula for the derivative of an inverse function, can be used to find the derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions.

learning_objectives.title: Selecting Procedures for Calculating Derivatives
learning_objectives.statement: This topic is intended to focus on the skill of selecting an appropriate procedure for calculating derivatives. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to calculating derivatives.
include: This topic is intended to focus on the skill of selecting an appropriate procedure for calculating derivatives. Students should be given opportunities to practice when and how to apply all learning objectives relating to calculating derivatives.

learning_objectives.title: Calculating Higher - Order Derivatives
learning_objectives.statement: Determine higher order derivatives of a function.
include: Determine higher order derivatives of a function.
Differentiating f ′ produces the second derivative f ″, provided the derivative of f ′ exists; repeating this process produces higherorder derivatives of f .

Higher-order derivatives are represented with a variety of notations. For y equals f of x), notations for the second derivative include d s quared y over d x squared comma f prime prime of x and y ″. Higher-order derivatives can be denoted n-th power y over d x to the n-th power.

learning_objectives.title: Interpreting the Meaning of the Derivative in Context
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret the meaning of a derivative in context.
include: Interpret the meaning of a derivative in context.
The derivative of a function can be interpreted as the instantaneous rate of change with respect to its independent variable.
The derivative can be used to express information about rates of change in applied contexts.
The unit for f'(x) is the unit for f divided by the unit for x.

learning_objectives.title: Straight-Line Motion: Connecting Position, Velocity, and Acceleration
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate rates of change in applied contexts.
include: Calculate rates of change in applied contexts.
The derivative can be used to solve rectilinear motion problems involving position, speed, velocity, and acceleration.

learning_objectives.title: Rates of Change in Applied Contexts Other Than Motion
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret rates of change in applied contexts.
include: Interpret rates of change in applied contexts.
The derivative can be used to solve problems involving rates of change in applied contexts.

learning_objectives.title: Introduction to Related Rates
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate related rates in applied contexts.
include: Calculate related rates in applied contexts.
The chain rule is the basis for differentiating variables in a related rates problem with respect to the same independent variable.
Other differentiation rules, such as the product rule and the quotient rule, may also be necessary to differentiate all variables with respect to the same independent variable.

learning_objectives.title: Solving Related Rates Problems
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret related rates in applied contexts.
include: Interpret related rates in applied contexts.
The derivative can be used to solve related rates problems; that is, finding a rate at which one quantity is changing by relating it to other quantities whose rates of change are known.

learning_objectives.title: Approximating Values of a Function Using Local Linearity and Linearization
learning_objectives.statement: Approximate a value on a curve using the equation of a tangent line. Determine limits of functions that result in indeterminate forms.
include: Approximate a value on a curve using the equation of a tangent line.
Determine limits of functions that result in indeterminate forms.
The tangent line is the graph of a locally linear approximation of the function near the point of tangency.

For a tangent line approximation, the function’s behavior near the point of tangency may determine whether a tangent line value is an underestimate or an overestimate of the corresponding function value.
When the ratio of two functions tends to 0 over fraction with numerator normal infinity and denominator normal infinityin the limit, such forms are said to be indeterminate.
Limits of the indeterminate forms 0 over e fraction with numerator normal infinity and denominator normal infinitymay be evaluated using L’Hospital’s Rule.
exclude: There are many other indeterminate forms, such asno r mal infinity minus normal infinity, for example, but these will not be assessed on either the AP Calculus AB or BC Exam. However, teachers may include these topics, if time permits.

learning_objectives.title: Using the Mean Value Theorem
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about functions by applying the Mean Value Theorem over an interval.
include: Justify conclusions about functions by applying the Mean Value Theorem over an interval.

If a function f is continuous over the interval [a, b] and differentiable over the interval (a, b), then the Mean Value Theorem guarantees a point within that open interval where the instantaneous rate of change equals the average rate of change over the interval.

learning_objectives.title: Extreme Value Theorem, Global Versus Local Extrema, and Critical Points
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about functions by applying the Extreme Value Theorem.
include: Justify conclusions about functions by applying the Extreme Value Theorem.
If a function f is continuous over the interval [a, b], then the Extreme Value Theorem guarantees that f has at least one minimum value and at least one maximum value on [a, b].
A point on a function where the first derivative equals zero or fails to exist is a critical point of the function.
All local (relative) extrema occur at critical points of a function, though not all critical points are local extrema.

learning_objectives.title: Determining Intervals on Which a Function Is Increasing or Decreasing
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
The first derivative of a function can provide information about the function and its graph, including intervals where the function is increasing or decreasing.

learning_objectives.title: Using the First Derivative Test to Determine Relative (Local) Extrema
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
The first derivative of a function can determine the location of relative (local) extrema of the function.

learning_objectives.title: Using the Candidates Test to Determine Absolute (Global) Extrema
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
Absolute (global) extrema of a function on a closed interval can only occur at critical points or at endpoints.

learning_objectives.title: Determining Concavity of Functions over Their Domains
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
The graph of a function is concave up (down) on an open interval if the function’s derivative is increasing (decreasing) on that interval.
The second derivative of a function provides information about the function and its graph, including intervals of upward or downward concavity.
The second derivative of a function may be used to locate points of inflection for the graph of the original function.

learning_objectives.title: Using the Second Derivative Test to Determine Extrema
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
The second derivative of a function may determine whether a critical point is the location of a relative (local) maximum or minimum.

When a continuous function has only one critical point on an interval on its domain and the critical point corresponds to a relative (local) extremum of the function on the interval, then that critical point also corresponds to the absolute (global) extremum of the function on the interval.

learning_objectives.title: Sketching Graphs of Functions and Their Derivatives
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
Key features of functions and their derivatives can be identified and related to their graphical, numerical, and analytical representations.
Graphical, numerical, and analytical information from f' and f" can be used to predict and explain the behavior of f.

learning_objectives.title: Connecting a Function, Its First Derivative, and Its Second Derivative
learning_objectives.statement: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
include: Justify conclusions about the behavior of a function based on the behavior of its derivatives.
Key features of the graphs of f, f', and f" are related to one another.

learning_objectives.title: Introduction to Optimization Problems
learning_objectives.statement: Calculate minimum and maximum values in applied contexts or analysis of functions.
include: Calculate minimum and maximum values in applied contexts or analysis of functions.
The derivative can be used to solve optimization problems; that is, finding a minimum or maximum value of a function on a given interval.

learning_objectives.title: Solving Optimization Problems
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret minimum and maximum values calculated in applied contexts.
include: Interpret minimum and maximum values calculated in applied contexts.
Minimum and maximum values of a function take on specific meanings in applied contexts.

learning_objectives.title: Exploring Behaviors of Implicit Relations
learning_objectives.statement: Determine critical points of implicit relations. Justify conclusions about the behavior of an implicitly defined function based on evidence from its derivatives.
include: Determine critical points of implicit relations.
Justify conclusions about the behavior of an implicitly defined function based on evidence from its derivatives.
A point on an implicit relation where the first derivative equals zero or does not exist is a critical point of the function.
Applications of derivatives can be extended to implicitly defined functions.
Second derivatives involving implicit differentiation may be relations of x, y, and d

learning_objectives.title: Exploring Accumulations of Change
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret the meaning of areas associated with the graph of a rate of change in context.
include: Interpret the meaning of areas associated with the graph of a rate of change in context.
The area of the region between the graph of a rate of change function and the x axis gives the accumulation of change.
In some cases, accumulation of change can be evaluated by using geometry.
If a rate of change is positive (negative) over an interval, then the accumulated change is positive (negative).
The unit for the area of a region defined by rate of change is the unit for the rate of change multiplied by the unit for the independent variable.

learning_objectives.title: Approximating Areas with Riemann Sums
learning_objectives.statement: Approximate a definite integral using geometric and numerical methods.
include: Approximate a definite integral using geometric and numerical methods.
Definite integrals can be approximated for functions that are represented graphically, numerically, analytically, and verbally.

Definite integrals can be approximated using a left Riemann sum, a right Riemann sum, a midpoint Riemann sum, or a trapezoidal sum; approximations can be computed using either uniform or nonuniform partitions.
Definite integrals can be approximated using numerical methods, with or without technology.
Depending on the behavior of a function, it may be possible to determine whether an approximation for a definite integral is an underestimate or overestimate for the value of the definite integral.

learning_objectives.title: Riemann Sums, Summation Notation, and Definite Integral Notation
learning_objectives.statement: Interpret the limiting case of the Riemann sum as a definite integral. Represent the limiting case of the Riemann sum as a definite integral.
include: Interpret the limiting case of the Riemann sum as a definite integral.
Represent the limiting case of the Riemann sum as a definite integral.
The limit of an approximating Riemann sum can be interpreted as a definite integral.

A Riemann sum, which requires a partition of an interval I, is the sum of products, each of which is the value of the function at a point in a subinterval multiplied by the length of that subinterval of the partition.

The definite integral of a continuous function f over the interval [a, b], denoted integral from a to b of f of x d x is the limit of Riemann sums as the widths of the subintervals approach 0. That is, f of x d x equals lim over max of normal triangle x sub i right arrow 0 of the sum from i equals 1 to n of f of open paren x sub i raised to the asterisk power close paren normal triangle x sub the number of subintervals, normal triangle x sub i is the width of the ith subinterval, and x sub i raised to the asterisk power is a value in the ith subinterval.
A definite integral can be translated into the limit of a related Riemann sum, and the limit of a Riemann sum can be written as a definite integral.

learning_objectives.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and Accumulation Functions
learning_objectives.statement: Represent accumulation functions using definite integrals.
include: Represent accumulation functions using definite integrals.
The definite integral can be used to define new functions.
If f is a continuous function on an interval containing a, then d times open paren the integral from a to x of f of t d t close paren equals f of x where x is in the interval.

learning_objectives.title: Interpreting the Behavior of Accumulation Functions Involving Area
